scope: Proposition 6.5 (Quantitative marginal estimates) of the manuscript “Conditional information under deterministic coordinate sweeps” (preprints/Conditional-information-under-deterministic-coordinate-sweeps-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ad4125b0a60530a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The following choices give the indicated energy bounds uniformly over the sequential indices, and hence the corresponding large-marginal estimates. In each row q is fixed and at most n − n/q cards are observed. The letters Cfix, L, C, b0 denote fixed integers satisfying the displayed conditions. Input used q β γ Time and energy fixed 16 1/32 127/128 T = Cfixd, aT = O(n−6) fixed 8 1/16 63/64 T = 512d, aT = O(n−7) random 32 1/64 127/128 T = Ld, aT = O(n−10) random 8 1/16 31/32 T = 200d, aT = O(n−8) random 256 1/1024 2047/2048 T = Cd, aT = o(n−4) random 64 1/128 511/512 T = b0d, aT = O(n−5) random K = 8192 1/(2K) 1 − 1/(8K) T = (100K + 2)d, aT = o(n−4) The integer choices are (127/128)Cfix−2 ≤ 2−6 , (127/128)L−2 ≤ 2−10 , (2047/2048)C−2 < 2−4 , (511/512)b0−2 ≤ 2−5 . The first two rows will be used for prescribed lists, and the other rows on average over uniform initial lists. In fact the fixed-domain part of Lemma 6.3 also proves every energy bound in the table for each prescribed list: it has at least the displayed β and an exponentially small exceptional term. The distinction in the table records the information used by the transfers below. In particular the eight-block random-domain row has average marginal distance O(n−5/2), and the 64-block row has distance O(n−1).
